meta.name: Future Job Radar
meta.thesis: Technology is a net job creator. In 1995 nobody was an Uber driver, an Airbnb host or an influencer.

scans.headline: First scan: 44 jobs mapped
scans.summary: First radar build from analyst reports (WEF, ARK), futurists (Diamandis, Kurzweil, Webb), technologists (Musk, Huang, Altman, Amodei), live markets (Waymo, Optimus, humanoid games) and 40+ sci-fi references.

scans.headline: Star Trek scan: 22 new jobs from Starfleet and beyond
scans.summary: A deep dive into Star Trek, from Starfleet Academy (2026) to the holodeck, tricorder, replicator and Counselor Troi, plus Jurassic Park, Dune, Star Wars, Foundation and Minority Report. Matched with signals such as DeepMind's Genie 3, Project CETI, the 2025 Chemistry Nobel and Colossal's dire wolves.

scans.headline: Money at machine speed: finance and farming join the radar
scans.summary: AI agents now pay over stablecoin rails in seconds for fractions of a cent (x402, Google AP2, Visa and Mastercard agent payments, $315B in stablecoins, $39B in tokenized assets). Remixed with Snow Crash, Daemon, Nosedive, Interstellar's robot combines and The Ministry for the Future's carbon coin.

scans.headline: Cybercabs take paid rides, McKinsey counts more jobs created than lost, and AI data centres go underground like a real-life Silo
scans.summary: This week Tesla began paid Cybercab rides in Austin, Nevada cleared thousands of robotaxis for Las Vegas, McKinsey's new US study put jobs created (about 41 million) above jobs facing lower demand (about 36 million) by 2035, and BlackRock and Cloudflare pushed agent payments forward. The focus universes are Silo (life inside a giant buried machine) and Murderbot (care, security and contracts in a hyper-capitalist future), which gave us five jobs spanning curbs, caverns, compute neighbours, care robots and brain-to-voice.
scans.focus: Silo (Apple TV+) and The Murderbot Diaries, with a side look at Becky Chambers (Monk and Robot)

scans.headline: A million data-centre satellites could redraw the night sky, and someone has to negotiate it
scans.summary: This week's signals: Google flew its first TPU to orbit, astronomers modelled sky rings from orbital data centres, Germany now requires data-centre heat reuse, and humanoid safety rules are still unfinished. The focus universes are The Three-Body Problem (a sky that becomes contested) and Severance (memory split across a boundary).
scans.focus: The Three-Body Problem and Severance, with Asimov, Dune, Kim Stanley Robinson and Silo as supporting universes

jobs.day: He builds a pre-match film around two rival robot teams, plans a half-time drone show, and has a backup match ready in case a robot breaks down.
